beats: Hook: four workers on an assembly line, and for a big part of every shift most of them are standing around.
The cut: pipeline parallelism gives each GPU a run of layers; activations go forward, activation gradients come back, point to point.
Cheap talk: the work at a stage grows with h^2 but the handoff only with h: compute is 8x (forward) to 16x (backward) the communication on A100s.
The bubble: with one big batch only one station works at a time.
Micro-batches: split the batch into many small ones and the line fills up (all-forward-all-backward).
The catch: every station keeps each micro-batch's activations until its backward returns, so memory grows with M.
1F1B (PipeDream): start each backward as early as possible; stations only hold N, N-1, ..., 1 micro-batches in flight.
The formula: bubble = (N-1)/M for both schedules; 1F1B wins on memory, which buys more micro-batches.
Worked example: 3 stages, 3 micro-batches, a heavy first batch: 100% vs 83% bubble.
Takeaway: more stages means more bubble, and micro-batches cannot shrink below one sequence: you cannot cut a cupcake smaller (cliffhanger into L06-02).
Cover (line_cover_l06_01; for the X post and thumbnails, not a film beat): four bakers on one conveyor line: one works flat out while three stand around.
